subject: Calculus
text: The chain rule is used when one function is written inside another function. In composite functions, students should identify the outer function and inner function before differentiating. The derivative is found by differentiating the outer function first and then multiplying by the derivative of the inner function. A common student mistake is to apply only the power rule and ignore the inner expression. This leads to incomplete answers in exam questions. A good solving pattern is to first rewrite the expression mentally as f(g(x)), then apply the chain rule step by step.

subject: Calculus
text: Integration by parts is applied when the integrand contains a product of two terms and one of them becomes simpler after differentiation. The standard formula is integral of u dv equals u multiplied by v minus integral of v du. Students often use the LIATE idea to choose u. If u is chosen badly, the second integral becomes harder and the method fails. In exam preparation, students should practice deciding u and dv before starting the calculation.

subject: DSA
text: Big-O notation describes how the cost of an algorithm grows as input size increases. In most academic questions, students should identify the dominant loop or repeated operation and ignore constant factors. If one loop runs n times, the time complexity is usually O(n). If nested loops both run n times, the complexity is usually O(n squared). Students lose marks when they describe the algorithm in words but do not express the final growth rate correctly.

subject: DSA
text: A recursive function must always have a base case. The base case is the stopping condition that prevents infinite calls and stack overflow. It handles the smallest version of the problem directly. One reliable coding habit is to write the base case before writing the recursive step. This reduces logical errors and makes recursion easier to explain in viva or lab evaluation.

subject: Japanese
text: Vocabulary retention at the N4 level improves more through active recall than passive rereading. Students should test themselves on meaning, pronunciation, and sentence usage instead of only reviewing lists. Spaced repetition and repeated retrieval improve speed during viva and written exams. Short, frequent revision sessions are usually more effective than one long memorization session.

subject: PHP
text: Associative arrays in PHP store data using named keys instead of numeric indexes. They are useful when representing structured information such as student records, user details, or configuration values. Students commonly confuse associative arrays with indexed arrays. Because of that, they sometimes try to access values using numeric positions even when the array was built with named keys. In lab work, this causes undefined index errors and incorrect output.
